neutral_facts.value: The accused and his colleague were allegedly chased by the victim and his colleague after a quarrel at a hotel. The victim was assaulted with a weapon, resulting in his death. A police constable witnessed the incident and described the accused's clothing. Blood-stained clothes matching the victim's blood group were recovered from the accused shortly after the incident. The victim's dying declaration described the accused's clothing and the weapon used. The investigating officer confirmed the sequence of events and the recovery of evidence. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court reversed the acquittal, finding the evidence sufficient to establish the accused's guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The dying declaration Exh. 21 has a ring of truth. The deceased specifically deposed to the clothes worn by the assailant. PW-13, who witnessed the incident, corroborated the nature of the apparel worn by the accused. Clothes recovered from the appellant matched the description. Stains on the clothes matched the blood group of the deceased. Medical evidence is consistent with ocular evidence.

quotes.text: The dying declaration Exh. 21 has a ring of truth. The deceased specifically deposed to the clothes which were worn by the assailant. PW-13, who had witnessed the incident, corroborated the nature of the apparel worn by the accused/assailant. The clothes which were recovered from the appellant at the time of his arrest within a few hours of the incident, matched that description. Added to this, is the fact that the blood group on the stains which were found on the clothes, matched the blood group of the deceased. The identity of the appellant has been established beyond reasonable doubt. The medical evidence in regard to the nature of the injuries is entirely consistent with the ocular evidence.

witness_credibility.value: PW-13, the beat constable, was on duty and his presence at the incident location was natural. His statement that he was assigned to duty at the place of the incident was not cast in doubt. The mere fact that panch witnesses turned hostile is no reason to discredit the prosecution's case.

quotes.text: The presence of PW-13 at the spot where the incident took place was in the natural course of things. Nothing has been elicited in the course of his cross-examination to cast a doubt on his statement that he was assigned to duty at the place where the incident took place. Similarly, the mere fact that the panch witnesses in support of the discovery had turned hostile is no reason to discredit the case of the prosecution.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellant was the assailant, citing the dying declaration of the deceased, the testimony of PW-13 (the beat constable), the blood-stained clothes recovered from the appellant, and the medical evidence consistent with the ocular evidence. They also emphasized that the High Court correctly reversed the trial court's acquittal due to a miscarriage of justice.

quotes.text: The evidence of the beat constable on duty (PW -13); the dying declaration (Ex. 21); and the evidence of the investigating officer (PW-14).

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the trial court's acquittal was justified, citing discrepancies in the investigation, the lack of direct identification of the appellant by PW-13, the failure to conduct a test identification parade, the hostility of certain witnesses, and the absence of examination of key witnesses like Lt. Melvin Desouza and the accompanying beat constable.

quotes.text: Though the incident took place on the night of 10 July 1988 and the death of the victim occurred on 23 July 1988, no effort was made by the investigating officer to produce the accused before the victim for the purposes of identification.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that an appellate court is justified in reversing an order of acquittal if it suffers from perversity and results in a miscarriage of justice, as established in K Gopal Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh and Chandrappa v. State of Karnataka.

quotes.text: The appellate court is justified in reversing an order of acquittal where the order of acquittal suffers from a perversity and has resulted in a miscarriage of justice.

sentencing_rationale.value: The High Court convicted the appellant under Section 304 Part II of the IPC and sentenced him to five years' rigorous imprisonment because the incident was preceded by a quarrel, and thus did not attract the provisions of Section 302. The High Court found the charge against the appellant established beyond reasonable doubt.

quotes.text: The High Court on the basis of the evidence on the record came to the conclusion that since the incident had been preceded by a quarrel, the case would not attract the provisions of Section 302.
